title: Movement Symptoms
content: Parkinson's disease can affect movement in different ways. Important movement symptoms include bradykinesia, meaning slowness of movement, tremor and rigidity. Other movement changes can include reduced arm swing, smaller handwriting, stooped posture, shuffling steps, difficulty turning, freezing of gait and balance problems. Symptoms differ between individuals and may change as the condition progresses. Not everyone with Parkinson's experiences tremor. Movement symptoms should be interpreted together rather than using a single symptom to determine whether someone has Parkinson's disease.
